name: Northwest Nigeria banditry, Lakurawa and the Kainji-Borgu jihadist belt
started: 2025-12-25 (first US strikes in Nigeria, against IS-linked Lakurawa in Sokoto; banditry escalated from about 2011)
summary: Armed bandit gangs, now overlapping with Islamic State-linked Lakurawa, ISSP, JNIM and a Boko Haram cell, have made Nigeria's northwest and the Kainji-Borgu forests among the deadliest places in West Africa. Sokoto alone recorded more than 900 conflict deaths between July 2025 and June 2026, double the previous year (ACLED), and the Woro massacre in Kwara (Feb 2026) killed 162 to 200+. It is where the US carried out its first-ever strikes in Nigeria.

sides.name: Nigerian government
members: Police and state vigilante and community guard forces
backers: United States (Christmas 2025 strikes in Sokoto, ISR flights)

sides.name: Armed bandit groups
members: Fulani-led bandit gangs in Zamfara, Katsina, Sokoto, Kebbi, Niger and Kaduna states, e.g. the group of Kachalla Chimmo (Sokoto)
backers: Self-financed through ransom kidnapping, cattle theft and illegal mining levies
leaders: Kachalla Chimmo (named by ACLED for a June 2026 Sokoto attack)

sides.name: Jihadist groups in the northwest and Kainji-Borgu belt
members: Islamic State Sahel Province (first Nigerian claims since 2019 in 2026)
Boko Haram (JAS) cells in the Borgu forests
leaders: 'Sadiku', leader of the JAS cell blamed for the Woro massacre (Wikipedia)

background: Rural banditry in the northwest grew out of herder-farmer conflict, cattle rustling and illegal gold mining into an industry of mass kidnapping for ransom, with gangs taxing villages and fighting vigilantes. Since about 2023 jihadist actors have moved in: Lakurawa (fighters linked to IS Sahel) along the Niger border in Sokoto and Kebbi, JNIM and ISSP probing from Niger and Benin, and a Boko Haram cell in the Borgu forests near Kainji Lake.

Why it matters: the merging of criminal and jihadist networks gives jihadists cash and local reach, links the Sahel insurgency to Nigeria's heartland, and puts Abuja's capital region within reach. Mass school abductions keep the crisis in the national and international spotlight.
year: The window opened with JNIM's first claimed Nigerian attack (Nuku, Kwara, 28 Oct 2025) and a wave of abductions: 25 schoolgirls from a boarding school in Kebbi (15 Nov 2025), 38 worshippers in Eruku, Kwara (18 Nov) and 303 students and 12 teachers from St Mary's Catholic School, Papiri, Niger state (21 Nov), all later freed by 21 Dec. On 25 Dec US forces fired more than a dozen missiles at Lakurawa/IS targets in Sokoto. Attacks in 2026 included Kasuwan-Daji, Borgu (50 killed, 3 Jan), the abduction of about 177 worshippers in Kurmin Wali, Kaduna (18 Jan), the Woro and Nuku massacre in Kwara (3-4 Feb, 162 to 200+ killed), three Borgu villages (46 killed, 14 Feb), Lakurawa raids in Arewa LGA, Kebbi (34 killed, 18-19 Feb) and Tungan Dutse, Zamfara (50+ killed, 19 Feb). ISSP claimed attacks in Kebbi (24 Mar, 10 soldiers) and Sokoto (16 May, 7 soldiers), its first in Nigeria since 2019. An air strike at Tumfa, Zamfara killed at least 72 civilians on 10 May. June 2026 was the deadliest month on record in Sokoto. Lakurawa clashed with the Mahmuda group in Niger state in August.
situation: As of late October 2026 bandits dominate much of rural Zamfara, Katsina, Sokoto and western Niger state, with highway attacks and kidnappings continuing (Katsina residents protested in September). Lakurawa and ISSP operate along the Niger border in Sokoto and Kebbi; the Kainji-Borgu forests host overlapping jihadist cells. Government operations rely heavily on air power with repeated civilian casualties.
technical: First US strikes in Nigeria (25 Dec 2025): more than a dozen missiles hit Warriya, Alkasim and forest areas at Kawuri, Malgum and Bauni in Sokoto; some munitions landed elsewhere without detonating (ACLED). Nigeria called it a joint operation using Nigerian intelligence.
ACLED had recorded 56 Islamist-related political violence incidents in Sokoto since 2024, all attributed to Lakurawa, before the US strikes.

ISSP's first claimed Nigerian operations since 2019: near Giro Masa, Shanga LGA, Kebbi (24 Mar 2026, 10 soldiers killed) and near Rumji Dan Tudu, Illela LGA, Sokoto (16 May 2026, 7 soldiers killed) (ACLED).
Lakurawa coordinated raids on villages in Arewa LGA, Kebbi (18 Feb 2026) killed 34 and took cattle (Peoples Gazette).

Woro massacre attackers had sent warning letters, including one in Boko Haram's formal name and that of its Lake Chad leader Bakura Doro; soldiers requested earlier had withdrawn after weeks (Wikipedia, citing Amnesty).

Mass school abductions remain a signature tactic: Papiri (303 students, 12 teachers, Nov 2025), Kebbi boarding school (25 girls, Nov 2025), Askira/Uba (42 children, May 2026, northeast), Kaura Namoda students (June 2026).
Bandits use IEDs on roads: several devices on the Magami-Yar'Tasha-Dansadau highway in Zamfara killed at least 10 (27 Dec 2025).
Air-strike errors: Tumfa, Zamfara (10 May 2026, at least 72 civilians) and Niger state the same day (13 civilians) during anti-bandit operations (Wikipedia).
Pro-government militia abuses: a militia with Beninese vigilantes killed 41 Fulani herders in Borgu on 30 Apr 2026 (Wikipedia).
Jihadist-on-jihadist competition: Lakurawa clashed with Mahmuda militants around Dikera and Binzi, Niger state (22 Aug 2026).
casualties: ACLED: over 900 fatalities in Sokoto alone between July 2025 and June 2026, more than double the previous 12 months; June 2026 the deadliest month in Sokoto since 1997. Africa Center: Lakurawa accounted for 299 deaths in 2025. Major incidents: Woro and Nuku 162 (Red Cross) to 200+; Kasuwan-Daji 50; Tungan Dutse 50+; Borgu 46; Kebbi Arewa 34; Tumfa air strike 72+. Combined with Zamfara, Katsina and Niger state, the 12-month total is very likely well over 1,000 (inference).
displaced: No current figures retrieved. Residents fled Arewa LGA communities after the February 2026 Lakurawa raids (Peoples Gazette).

timeline.event: JNIM claims its first attack in Nigeria (Nuku, Kwara).
303 students and 12 teachers abducted from St Mary's, Papiri, Niger state.
Remaining St Mary's students and teachers freed.
US strikes IS-linked targets in Sokoto state.
About 177 worshippers abducted from three churches at Kurmin Wali, Kaduna.
Woro and Nuku massacre in Kwara begins (162 to 200+ killed).
Lakurawa raids in Kebbi (34 killed); 50+ killed at Tungan Dutse, Zamfara.
ISSP attack near Giro Masa, Kebbi kills 10 soldiers.
Air strike at Tumfa, Zamfara kills at least 72 civilians.
ISSP attack near Rumji Dan Tudu, Sokoto kills 7 soldiers.
Lakurawa and Mahmuda clash around Dikera and Binzi, Niger state.

outlook: Watch whether Lakurawa and ISSP keep expanding along the Niger border, whether JNIM deepens its presence in Kainji-Borgu, whether US strikes resume, and further mass school kidnappings. Peace deals with bandit leaders have repeatedly broken down.

zones.name: Sokoto-Kebbi border belt (Lakurawa, ISSP)
zones.note: Lakurawa camps; US strikes 25 Dec 2025; ISSP attacks in Shanga and Illela LGAs in 2026; Sokoto's record violence.

zones.name: Zamfara bandit heartland
zones.note: Mass kidnapping, highway IEDs, Tungan Dutse massacre (Feb 2026), Tumfa air strike (May 2026).

zones.name: Katsina frontier
zones.note: Bandit raids in Faskari and Jibia; residents protested rising attacks in Sept 2026.

zones.name: Kainji-Borgu forests (Niger and Kwara states)
zones.note: Overlap of JNIM, JAS cell, Lakurawa and Mahmuda; Woro massacre; Kasuwan-Daji and Borgu village attacks; Papiri abduction.

zones.name: Northern Kaduna (Kajuru, Kauru)
zones.note: Church attacks and mass abductions (Kurmin Wali, Jan 2026).

battles.name: Woro and Nuku massacre
battles.place: Woro and Nuku, Kaiama LGA, Kwara state, Nigeria
sides: Boko Haram (JAS) cell in the Borgu forests (blamed by Tinubu and analysts)
battles.outcome: Massacre; Operation Savanna Shield launched in response.
battles.forces: Jihadist gunmen attacking from about 17:30 to about 03:00.
battles.losses: 162 killed (Red Cross, state officials), later reported over 200; 38 abducted; about 38 homes and the Woro ruler's palace destroyed. About 95% of victims reportedly Muslim.
battles.significance: One of Nigeria's deadliest single attacks in years, far from the northeast, showing jihadist reach into the Kainji-Borgu belt near Benin.

battles.name: US strikes on Islamic State-linked camps in Sokoto
battles.place: Warriya, Alkasim and Kawuri, Malgum and Bauni forests near Jabo, Sokoto state, Nigeria (coordinates approximate)
battles.outcome: Strikes carried out; US claimed multiple militants killed; some munitions failed to detonate.
battles.forces: More than a dozen ship-launched missiles (ACLED; Pentagon video).
battles.losses: US: 'multiple' ISIS fatalities (unverified); a local witness denied fighters were killed.
battles.significance: The first US strikes in Nigeria in ACLED's records since 1997; opened a phase of direct US military involvement.

battles.name: St Mary's Catholic School abduction, Papiri
battles.place: Papiri, Agwara LGA, Niger state, Nigeria (coordinates approximate)
battles.outcome: 50 students escaped within two days; the remaining 130 students and teachers were freed by 21 Dec 2025.
battles.losses: 303 students and 12 teachers abducted (Wikipedia, 2025 in Nigeria).
battles.significance: One of the largest school abductions in Nigeria's history; it came amid US 'Christian persecution' claims and fed pressure for US action.
